title: Microsoft SharePoint Online: Classic publishing restrictions begin March 1, 2027
summary: Starting March 1, 2027, SharePoint Online will block creation and activation of classic publishing sites and features, enforcing restrictions on custom scripting. New tenants face additional limits on classic pages. Administrators must update workflows and modernize pages before the rollout completes by October 2028.
body:
[What and why]

As previously announced in MC1464926, we are introducing restrictions on classic publishing and custom scripting in SharePoint Online to reduce security and governance risks associated with legacy customization. Beginning March 1, 2027, we will block the creation of new classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites across all tenants. Administrators will no longer be able to override these restrictions using the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting.

This reminder outlines the changes taking effect on March 1, 2027, and the steps administrators should take to prepare.

[Rollout schedule]

- General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in early March 2027 and is expected to complete by early October 2028.[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- All SharePoint Online tenants.- Administrators managing classic publishing sites, custom scripts, provisioning automation, and migration workflows.- Tenants created on or after March 1, 2027, which will have additional restrictions.Platforms and services

- SharePoint OnlineWhat will happen

All tenants, beginning March 1, 2027:

- SharePoint Online will block the creation of classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites.- SharePoint Online will enforce the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting as False. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.Additional restrictions for tenants created on or after March 1, 2027:

- Users will no longer be able to create or edit classic user-created pages or add or update custom scripts.- SharePoint Online will enforce the DenyAddAndCustomizePages site setting as True. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.- The Allow users to create new modern pages setting in SharePoint admin center > Settings > Pages will be enabled and cannot be disabled.- This modern-page setting change will not affect existing tenants.Classic user-created pages in scope:

- Affected pages include wiki, Web Part, blog, publishing, and custom ASPX pages.- List and library views and list form pages are excluded from the page read-only change.- Custom scripts embedded in these experiences will remain subject to scripting restrictions when the applicable phase takes effect.[Action required and recommendations]

Before March 1, 2027:

- Identify provisioning automation and migration plans that create classic publishing site collections or subsites or activate publishing features.- Update affected workflows to use modern alternatives.To prepare for October 1, 2028, we recommend that existing tenants:

- Review the requirements for the classic pages assessment.- Inventory classic pages using the Microsoft 365 Assessment Tool and assign modernization owners.- Pilot the transformation of classic SharePoint pages to modern pages. Transformation approaches vary by page type, and customized pages may require rebuilding.[Learn more]

- Requirements for the classic pages assessment | Microsoft Learn- Transform classic SharePoint pages to modern pages | Microsoft Learn
bodyHtml:
[What and why]

As previously announced in MC1464926, we are introducing restrictions on classic publishing and custom scripting in SharePoint Online to reduce security and governance risks associated with legacy customization. Beginning March 1, 2027, we will block the creation of new classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites across all tenants. Administrators will no longer be able to override these restrictions using the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting.

This reminder outlines the changes taking effect on March 1, 2027, and the steps administrators should take to prepare.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in early March 2027 and is expected to complete by early October 2028.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All SharePoint Online tenants.
  • Administrators managing classic publishing sites, custom scripts, provisioning automation, and migration workflows.
  • Tenants created on or after March 1, 2027, which will have additional restrictions.

Platforms and services

  • SharePoint Online

What will happen

All tenants, beginning March 1, 2027:

  • SharePoint Online will block the creation of classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites.
  • SharePoint Online will enforce the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting as False. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.

Additional restrictions for tenants created on or after March 1, 2027:

  • Users will no longer be able to create or edit classic user-created pages or add or update custom scripts.
  • SharePoint Online will enforce the DenyAddAndCustomizePages site setting as True. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.
  • The Allow users to create new modern pages setting in SharePoint admin center > Settings > Pages will be enabled and cannot be disabled.
  • This modern-page setting change will not affect existing tenants.

Classic user-created pages in scope:

  • Affected pages include wiki, Web Part, blog, publishing, and custom ASPX pages.
  • List and library views and list form pages are excluded from the page read-only change.
  • Custom scripts embedded in these experiences will remain subject to scripting restrictions when the applicable phase takes effect.

[Action required and recommendations]

Before March 1, 2027:

  • Identify provisioning automation and migration plans that create classic publishing site collections or subsites or activate publishing features.
  • Update affected workflows to use modern alternatives.

To prepare for October 1, 2028, we recommend that existing tenants:

  • Review the requirements for the classic pages assessment.
  • Inventory classic pages using the Microsoft 365 Assessment Tool and assign modernization owners.
  • Pilot the transformation of classic SharePoint pages to modern pages. Transformation approaches vary by page type, and customized pages may require rebuilding.

[Learn more]

  • Requirements for the classic pages assessment | Microsoft Learn
  • Transform classic SharePoint pages to modern pages | Microsoft Learn
